summary: RSV-1..9 genuinely delivered, not asserted. Exactly one write path (appendReviewSurfaceViolation -> writeViolations appending to existing entries), no delete/update; pr-manager and orchestrator are read-only consumers. Corrupt/non-array ledgers throw a typed unreadable error surfaced as a counted acknowledgeable violation, never read as empty; absent ledger reads clean (correct backward-compat split). RSV-8 substitution detection is real pointer reconciliation (lifecycle surface_violation_id/ids cross-checked against ledger violation_ids; orphans reported under a distinct missing:<id> namespace so a prior acknowledgement cannot cover an erasure); unreadable-pointers state blocks instead of reading as agreement. Idempotency covered at both layers: close_operation_idempotency_key short-circuit before the append plus a deterministic sha256 violation_id. Executed the ledger + orchestrator suites: 49/49 green; the strongest tests (concurrent Promise.all append, well-formed empty-ledger substitution, acknowledged-then-erased, real pr prepare block-then-clear through runCli) are genuinely falsifying against real git repos and the real CLI. One low reporting-only finding: an idempotency-key replay of a close that recorded a violation reports surface_violation null and the rendered summary omits the violation block; the ledger, lifecycle pointers, gate, and review violations output all remain correct, so nothing can be laundered through it.

inspection.summary: Read all 16 changed paths at depth (the 953-line unit suite: titles enumerated, ~5 load-bearing bodies read verbatim, whole file executed). risk_surfaces=gate_orchestration. Attacks: (a) append-only: grepped every writer of surface-violations.json across src/, test/, bin/; writeViolations private with one caller; appendReviewSurfaceViolation called only from recordReviewSurfaceViolationForClose in agent-review.js; no truncate/rewrite path. (b) fail-closed: readReviewSurfaceViolations 47-73: ENOENT reads clean, JSON.parse failure and non-array entries throw VIBEPRO_REVIEW_SURFACE_LEDGER_UNREADABLE; readReviewSurfaceViolationSummary converts only that code to a blocking summary so pr prepare cannot pass on corruption. (c) RSV-8: reconcileReviewSurfaceViolationPointers 192-227 is a real set-difference over lifecycle pointers with a distinct missing:<id> namespace; readStoryLifecyclePointers applies strict failure policy closing the one-malformed-byte bypass. (d) idempotency: dedup key checked before append (agent-review.js 1002-1004); keyed replay neither duplicates nor re-appends; unkeyed replay dies on already-closed guard. (e) executed node --test on ledger+orchestrator suites: 49/49; concurrency test fails without the mkdir lock; RSV-8 tests assert exact orphan id and kind; RSV-5 drives real pr prepare artifact. (f) locks: ledger uses story-level .surface-violations.lock with read-modify-write fully inside it; append vs lifecycle pointer stamp non-atomicity resolves fail-closed and is documented in architecture doc and Spec residual risk. Backward compat: buildReviewSurfaceIntegrityGate fails only when unacknowledged>0, so no-ledger and legacy-lifecycle repos pass; legacy counted as unevaluated_lifecycle_count so pass reason never overclaims. New gate node has incoming+outgoing edges, registered in nodes, requiredGates, collectUnresolvedRequiredGates. listExistingReviewStages filtered by REVIEW_STAGES so the lock dir cannot be mistaken for a stage. All close callers after assertRecognizedCloseReason verified migrated.

judgment_delta: initial expected needs_changes (a 343-line append-only claim plus a new always-on required gate usually hides a rewrite path, a lenient-read bypass, or a backward-compat block) -> final pass because every attack landed on an explicit control exercised by an executed test: single-writer grep clean, parse path rejects rather than empties, RSV-8 is real pointer reconciliation with a separate acknowledgement namespace, strict-vs-lenient lifecycle reader split closes the one-byte bypass, gate fails only on unacknowledged entries so legacy repos are unaffected, acknowledgement route proven through the real pr prepare CLI. The expected non-atomicity between ledger append and pointer stamp resolves fail-closed and is a documented boundary, not a defect.
